# Declock {#declock .hiddenheading}

My website provides many examples of the [Quarto](https://quarto.org) publishing and the [Dec](/dec) measurement systems in action. I leverage Quarto support for the [Observable](https://observablehq.com/) data analysis and visualization system to create animated and interactive graphics like the [bar📊charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_chart) clocks🕓, [solar☀️terminator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminator_%28solar%29#:~:text=a%20moving%20line%20that%20divides%20the%20daylit%20side%20and%20the%20dark%20night%20side%20of%20a%20planetary%20body) map🗺, [Earth🌍orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth%27s_orbit) diagram, and [daylight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daylight#:~:text=the%20combination%20of%20all%20direct%20and%20indirect%20sunlight%20during%20the%20daytime) [area chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_chart#:~:text=The%20area%20between%20axis%20and%20line%20are%20commonly%20emphasized%20with%20colors) below.

::: {.column-margin .clocks #onlymargin .posneg}
\${posclock}\${negclock}
:::

This article focuses on the Dec clock (Declock) [metric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_time#:~:text=the%20measure%20of%20time%20intervals%20using%20the%20metric%20system) [decimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal_time#:~:text=the%20representation%20of%20the%20time%20of%20day%20using%20units%20which%20are%20decimally%20related) [time standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_standard#:~:text=a%20specification%20for%20measuring%20time), but also builds on the Dec [calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calendar#:~:text=a%20system%20of%20organizing%20days) (Decalendar) described in [the previous article](dec/date) in my series on the Dec measurement system. Together, Decalendar and Declock render months, fortnights, weeks, hours, minutes, and [International System of Units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_System_of_Units#:~:text=the%20world%27s%20most%20widely%20used%20system%20of%20measurement) ([SI](#si){#internationalsystemofunits .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="International System of Units"}) seconds ([sis](#sis){#sisecond .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="SI seconds"}) obsolete.

Declock measures time in [fractional days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal_time#Fractional_days:~:text=a%20decimal%20fraction%20of%20a%20day), often using [metric prefixes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_prefix#:~:text=a%20unit%20prefix%20that%20precedes%20a%20basic%20unit%20of%20measure%20to%20indicate%20a%20multiple%20or%20submultiple%20of%20the%20unit) like [deci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deci-#:~:text=a%20decimal%20unit%20prefix%20in%20the%20metric%20system%20denoting%20a%20factor%20of%20one%20tenth), [centi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centi-#:~:text=a%20unit%20prefix%20in%20the%20metric%20system%20denoting%20a%20factor%20of%20one%20hundredth), or [milli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milli-#:~:text=a%20unit%20prefix%20in%20the%20metric%20system%20denoting%20a%20factor%20of%20one%20thousandth). The top, middle, and bottom bars indicate the [decidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal_time#:~:text=dividing%20the%20day%20into%2010%20decidays){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="tenths of a day"}, [millidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_of_time#:~:text=1.44%20minutes%2C%20or%2086.4%20seconds){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="thousandths of a day"}, and [centimillidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal_time#:~:text=which%20would%20be-,1/100%2C000%20day,-%2C%20or%20864%20milliseconds){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hundred thousandths of a day"}, respectively, of the time since the start, \${decPosHsl()}, or until the end, \${decNegHsl()}, of the day in the Zone \${decZoneHsl}, the Dec [time zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_zone#:~:text=an%20area%20which%20observes%20a%20uniform%20standard%20time) selected by the red⭕️circle on the map beneath the bars.

To rotate the globe🌐in the Earth🌏orbit diagram, drag the red circle horizontally↔️or slide the red🔴dot on the daylight area chart vertically↕. The red circle's vertical position determines the yearly daylight pattern visualized by the area chart. Shift the vertical red<font color=red>—</font>line on the area chart horizontally to move the globe along the ellipse of the Earth🌎orbit.

{{< include /dec/time/_timecharts.qmd >}}

# Annual day aggregate (ada) {#sec-ada .hiddenheading}

The red line indicates a "day of year" ([doy](#doy){#dayofyear .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"}): \${selDateHsl()}, which identifies a day in a year like a [Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_calendar#:~:text=the%20calendar%20used%20in%20most%20parts%20of%20the%20world) month and "day of month" ([dom](#dom){#dayofmonth .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of month"}). The red dot denotes a "time of day" ([tod](#tod){#timeofday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"}): \${selTimeDay()}, which specifies a point in a day like an "hour minute second" ([hms](#hms){#hourminutesecond .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hour minute second"}) triplet. Together, a [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"} and [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} can form an "annual day aggregate" ([ada](#ada){#annualdayaggregate .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="annual day aggregate"}): \${selDateHsl()} + \${selTimeDay()} &div; 1000 = \${selDatePadHsl()}.\${selTimeMilDay()}.

::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup00}
$$
\begin{split}
\text{doy} &= \lfloor\text{ada}\rfloor \\
&= \text{ada} - \text{tod}
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-ada}
:::

As their names suggest, [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of year"} and [ada](#ada){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="annual day aggregates"} are measured in days. The [measurement unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_of_measurement#:~:text=a%20definite%20magnitude%20of%20a%20quantity) of a [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} can be a day or a [submultiple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_%28mathematics%29#Submultiple:~:text=of%20%22a%20being-,a%20unit%20fraction,-of%20b%22%20) of a day with a metric prefix. By changing how a decimal [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} is measured, we can shift its [decimal separator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal_separator#:~:text=a%20symbol%20that%20separates%20the%20integer%20part%20from%20the%20fractional%20part%20of%20a%20number) or turn it into an integer. The [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="times of day"} along the y-axis of the area chart are integers because they have three digits and are measured in [millidays]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="thousandths of a day"}.

# Epochal day aggregate (eda) {#sec-eda .hiddenheading}

To obtain a [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} from an [ada](#ada){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="annual day aggregate"}, we can [keep the remainder after dividing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) by one to isolate the [decimal part](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractional_part#:~:text=the%20excess%20beyond%20that%20number%27s%20integer%20part) of the [quotient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quotient#:~:text=a%20quantity%20produced%20by%20the%20division%20of%20two%20numbers): \${zeroDotyHsl()}.\${zeroTpadHsl()} [[&LeftFloor;]{.hyphen}](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) 1 = 0.\${zeroTpadHsl()}. We can use this same approach to separate a [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} from an "epochal day aggregate" ([eda](#eda){#epochaldayaggregate .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="epochal day aggregate"}): \${zeroDoteHsl}.\${zeroTpadHsl()} [&LeftFloor;]{.hyphen} 1 = 0.\${zeroTpadHsl()}. The current [eda](#eda){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="epochal day aggregate"} tells us how many days have passed since the Dec [epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epoch#:~:text=an%20instant%20in%20time%20chosen%20as%20the%20origin%20of%20a%20particular%20calendar%20era): Year [0]{.color0} Day [0]{.color0} [Tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} [0]{.color0}.

::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup01}

$$\text{dividend} \href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder%20or%20signed%20remainder%20of%20a%20division}{\mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}}} \text{modulus} = \text{dividend} - \text{modulus} \times \left\lfloor\dfrac{\text{dividend}}{\text{modulus}}\right\rfloor$$ {#eq-modulus}

$$\begin{split}
\text{tod} &= \text{ada} \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}} 1 \\
&= \text{eda} \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}} 1
\end{split}$$ {#eq-tod}
:::

## UNIX time equation {#sec-ute .unnumbered .hiddenheading}

Similarly, [UNIX time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time#:~:text=the%20number%20of%20non%2Dleap%20seconds%20that%20have%20elapsed%20since%2000%3A00%3A00%20UTC%20on%201%C2%A0January%201970%2C%20the%20Unix%20epoch) tallies the seconds since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time#:~:text=00%3A00%3A00%20UTC%20on%201%C2%A0January%201970), which is exactly 719468 days after the Dec epoch. To get the [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} in Zone [0]{.color0}, the Dec time zone that is in between the two leftmost vertical lines on the map, we can divide UNIX time by the [number of seconds in a day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day#:~:text=average%2C%20this%20is-,24%20hours%20(86%2C400%20seconds),-.%20As%20a%20day) and then keep the remainder after dividing the resulting days by 1 as in @eq-unixtod.

::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup02}
$$\text{tod} = \text{unix} \div 86400 \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}} 1$$ {#eq-unixtod}
:::

## Julian date equation {#sec-jde .unnumbered .hiddenheading}

[Julian dates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_day#:~:text=the%20Julian%20day%20number%20plus%20the%20fraction%20of%20a%20day%20since%20the%20preceding%20noon) track the days since the beginning of the [Julian period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_day#:~:text=a%20chronological%20interval%20of%207980%C2%A0years%2C%20derived%20from%20three%20multi%2Dyear%20cycles:%20the%20Indiction%2C%20Solar%2C%20and%20Lunar%20cycles) and thus are akin to [eda](#eda){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="epochal day aggregates"}. We can produce a Zone [5]{.color5} [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} from a [Julian date](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_day#:~:text=the%20Julian%20day%20number%20plus%20the%20fraction%20of%20a%20day%20since%20the%20preceding%20noon) simply by keeping the remainder after dividing by one. If we want a Zone [0]{.color0} [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} instead, we should add [5]{.color5} [decidays]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="tenths of a day"} to the Julian date, divide the sum by one, and then keep the remainder as in @eq-juliantod below.

::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup03}
$$\text{tod} = (\text{julian} + 0.5) \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}} 1$$ {#eq-juliantod}
:::

# Hour minute second (hms) {#sec-hms .hiddenheading}

We can also obtain a Zone [0]{.color0} [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} from a [Coordinated Universal Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time#:~:text=the%20primary%20time%20standard%20globally%20used%20to%20regulate%20clocks%20and%20time) ([UTC](#utc){#coordinateduniversaltime .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Coordinated Universal Time"}) [hms](#hms){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hour minute second"} triplet by summing its components after converting them to fractional days, as shown in the equation below. The [computer programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming#:~:text=the%20composition%20of%20sequences%20of%20instructions%2C%20called%20programs%2C%20that%20computers%20can%20follow%20to%20perform%20tasks) code in the [tabset panel](https://quarto.org/docs/interactive/layout.html#tabset-panel) beneath the equation compares [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="times of day"} derived from [UTC](#utc){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Coordinated Universal Time"} and UNIX time as Quarto was [rendering](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/hello/rstudio.html#rendering:~:text=When%20rendering%2C%20Quarto%20generates%20a%20new%20file%20that%20contains%20selected%20text%2C%20code%2C%20and%20results) this webpage.

::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup04}
$$\text{tod} = \dfrac{\text{hour}}{24} + \dfrac{\text{minute}}{1440} + \dfrac{\text{second}}{86400}$$ {#eq-hmstod}
:::

:::{.panel-tabset group="language"}
### Julia

```{julia}
using Dates
hms = now(UTC)
hour(hms) / 24 +
minute(hms) / 1440 +
second(hms) / 86400 +
millisecond(hms) / 864e5
datetime2unix(hms) / 86400 % 1
```

### Observable JavaScript

```{ojs}
hms = new Date();
hms.getUTCHours() / 24 +
hms.getUTCMinutes() / 1440 +
hms.getUTCSeconds() / 86400 +
hms.getUTCMilliseconds() / 864e5;
hms.getTime() / 864e5 % 1;
```

### Python

```{python}
from datetime import datetime, timezone
hms = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
hms.hour / 24 + \
hms.minute / 1440 + \
hms.second / 86400 + \
hms.microsecond / 864e8
hms.timestamp() / 86400 % 1
```

### R

```{r}
hms <- as.POSIXlt(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC")
hms$hour / 24 +
hms$min / 1440 +
hms$sec / 86400
(as.numeric(as.POSIXct(hms)) / 86400) %% 1
```

:::

Equations -@eq-dsa to -@eq-sisom below convert UNIX time or a Zone [0]{.color0} [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} into the three components of an [hms](#hms){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hour minute second"} triplet: the "hour of day" ([hod](#hod){#hourofday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hour of day"}), "minute of hour" ([moh](#moh){#minuteofhour .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="minute of hour"}), and "SI second of minute" ([sisom](#sisom){#sisecondofminute .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="SI second of minute"}), using a "daily second aggregate" ([dsisa](#dsa){#dailysecondaggregate .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="daily second aggregate"}) and "hourly second aggregate" ([hsisa](#hsa){#hourlysecondaggregate .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hourly second aggregate"}). While both count seconds, [dsisa](#dsa){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="daily second aggregates"} start at midnight ([Tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} [0]{.color0}) and [hsa](#hsa){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hourly second aggregates"} begin at the [top of the hour](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/top_of_the_hour).

::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup05}
$$\begin{split}
\text{dsa} & = \text{tod} \times 86400 \\
& = \text{unix} \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}}  86400
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-dsa}
$$
\text{hsa} = \text{dsa} \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}}  3600
$$ {#eq-hsa}
$$
\text{hod} = \lfloor \text{dsa} \div 3600 \rfloor
$$ {#eq-hod}
$$
\text{moh} = \lfloor \text{hsa} \div 60 \rfloor
$$ {#eq-moh}
$$
\text{sisom} = \lfloor \text{hsa} \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}}  60 \rfloor
$$ {#eq-sisom}
:::


:::{.panel-tabset group="language"}
### Julia

```{julia}
using Dates
dsa = datetime2unix(now(UTC)) / 86400 % 1 * 86400
hsa = dsa % 3600
map(x -> floor(Int, x), (dsa / 3600, hsa / 60, hsa % 60))
```

### Observable JavaScript

```{ojs}
dsa = Date.now() / 864e5 % 1 * 86400;
hsa = dsa % 3600;
[dsa / 3600, hsa / 60, hsa % 60].map(Math.floor)
```

### Python

```{python}
from datetime import datetime, timezone
dsa = datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp() / 86400 % 1 * 86400
hsa = dsa % 3600
tuple(map(int, [dsa // 3600, hsa // 60, hsa % 60 // 1]))
```

### R

```{r}
dsa <- (as.numeric(as.POSIXct(Sys.time())) / 86400) %% 1 * 86400
hsa <- dsa %% 3600
sapply(c(dsa %/% 3600, hsa %/% 60, hsa %% 60), as.integer)
```

:::

# Universal time offset (uto) {#sec-uto .hiddenheading}

The [Global Positioning System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Positioning_System#:~:text=a%20satellite%2Dbased%20hyperbolic%20navigation%20system), [BeiDou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BeiDou#:~:text=a%20satellite%2Dbased%20radio%20navigation%20system), and [Galileo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_(satellite_navigation)#:~:text=a%20global%20navigation%20satellite%20system%20(GNSS)%20created%20by%20the%20European%20Union) [global navigation satellite systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite_navigation#:~:text=a%20satellite%20navigation%20system%20with%20global%20coverage) along with most --- if not all --- [programming languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language#:~:text=a%20system%20of%20notation%20for%20writing%20source%20code%20such%20as%20used%20to%20produce%20a%20computer%20program) do not account for [leap seconds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leap_second#:~:text=one%2Dsecond%20adjustment), which appears to be for the best given that leap seconds [can cause problems](https://www.nist.gov/pml/time-and-frequency-division/leap-seconds-faqs#:~:text=detriments%20to%20adding%20leap%20seconds) and will be abolished no later than [2027]{.color27by100}+[081]{.color081by366} according to the [International Bureau of Weights and Measures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bureau_of_Weights_and_Measures#:~:text=an%20intergovernmental%20organisation%20(IGO)%2C%20through%20which%20its%2067%20member%2Dstates%20act%20on%20measurement%20standards).

On or before the deadline to abolish leap seconds, the tolerance for disagreement between [UTC](#utc){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Coordinated Universal Time"} and [Universal Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Time#Versions:~:text=a%20time%20standard%20based%20on%20Earth%27s%20rotation) ([UT](#ut){#universaltime .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Universal Time"}) will increase from [0.9375 Dec seconds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leap_second#:~:text=a%20maximum%20permitted%20variance%20of%20%C2%B10.9%20seconds) ([s](#s){#second .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"}) to 3750 [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"}. Since [1972]{.color72by100}+[122]{.color122by365}, only [27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leap_second#:~:text=27%20leap%20seconds%20have%20been%20added%20to%20UTC) leap seconds have been inserted, which is 0.75% of 3750 [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"}, and at this rate it will take over five millennia for the disparity between [UT](#ut){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Universal Time"} and [UTC](#utc){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Coordinated Universal Time"} to reach 3750 [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"}.

Instead of leap seconds, Dec matches [UT](#ut){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Universal Time"} using a "[universal time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Time#:~:text=a%20time%20standard%20based%20on%20Earth%27s%20rotation) [offset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC_offset#:~:text=the%20difference%20in%20hours%20and%20minutes%20between%20Coordinated%20Universal%20Time%20(UTC)%20and%20the%20standard%20time%20at%20a%20particular%20place)" ([uto](#uto){#universaltimeoffset .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="universal time offset"}). With the [leap second insertion dates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leap_second#:~:text=Announced%20leap%20seconds%20to%20date) provided by the [International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Earth_Rotation_and_Reference_Systems_Service#:~:text=the%20body%20responsible%20for%20maintaining%20global%20time%20and%20reference%20frame%20standards), we can approximate the [uto](#uto){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="universal time offset"} that yields [UT](#ut){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Universal Time"} when added to the Zone [0]{.color0} [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} on the [Dec date](/dec/date) chosen by the [range](https://observablehq.com/framework/inputs/range)🎚️inputs below: \${leapCountHsl} &div; 8640 = \${leapSdecHsl()}\${leapSb24hsl()} &div; 90000 = \${leapTzoHsl()}.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| label: dateinput
//| class: slider
viewof leapSecondYear = Inputs.range([1970, 2020], {label: "Year", value: 1995, step: 1})
viewof leapSecondDate = Inputs.range([0, 365], {label: "Day", value: 182, step: 1})
```

# Second interval difference (sid) {#sec-sid .hiddenheading}

The equation above divides leap seconds by the number of sis or Dec [deciseconds]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="tenths of a second"} ([ds](#ds){#decisecond .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec deciseconds"}) in a [deciday]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="tenth of a day"} ([dd](#dd){#deciday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="deciday"}): 8640 [sis](#sis){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="SI seconds"} = 90000 [ds](#ds){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec deciseconds"} = 1 [dd](#dd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="deciday"}. To avoid [repeating decimals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repeating_decimal#:~:text=the%20same%20sequence%20of%20digits%20is%20repeated%20forever) when turning [sis](#sis){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="SI seconds"} into [ds](#ds){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec deciseconds"}, we can put a Dec [quadravigesimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_numeral_systems#:~:text=24-,Quadravigesimal,-%5B48%5D) ([base24]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="quadravigesimal"}) digit in place of the ones digit and decimal part of the [ds](#ds){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec deciseconds"}: \${leapSdecHsl()}\${leapSb24hsl()} = \${leapSdecHsl()} &times; 10 + \${leapSsidHsl} &div; 2.4.

Known as a "second interval difference" ([sid](#sid){#secondintervaldifference .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="second interval difference"}), the [base24]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="quadravigesimal"} ([b24](#b24){#base24 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base24"}) character at the end of \${leapSdecHsl()}\${leapSb24hsl()} is a letter of the [Greek alphabet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_alphabet#:~:text=the%20writing%20system%20used%20for%20the%20Greek%20language). To display [sis](#sis){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="SI seconds"} in [ds](#ds){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec deciseconds"}, we can concatenate the integer part of the [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"} we obtain from @eq-sis with the [b24](#b24){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base24"} representation of the [sid](#sid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="second interval difference"} we get from @eq-sid. The table beneath these equations lists [base10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal#:~:text=a%20numeral%20system%20that%20uses%20ten%20as%20its%20radix%20%28base%29) ([b10](#b10){#base10 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base10"}) and [b24](#b24){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base24"} equivalents.

::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup06}
$$
\text{s} = \dfrac{\text{ds}}{10} = \dfrac{\text{sis}}{0.96}
$$ {#eq-sis}
$$
\begin{split}
\text{sid} &= \text{sis} \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}} 24\\
&= (\text{s} - \text{sis}) \times 24 \mathbin{-\mkern-3.5mu\raise{0.073em}{\scriptstyle\lfloor}} 24
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-sid}
:::

## Base9 {#sec-b9 .unnumbered .hiddenheading}

Whereas [b24](#b24){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base24"} is like glue that allows us to combine [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"} and [sid](#sid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="second interval differences"}, Dec [nonary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ternary_numeral_system#Compact_ternary_representation:_base_9_and_27:~:text=base%209%2C%20each%20digit%20is%20two%20ternary%20digits) ([base9]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="nonary"}) enables us to append [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"} to a [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"}. The table below shows the [astronomical symbols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronomical_symbol#:~:text=symbols%20used%20to%20represent%20astronomical%20objects) used by Dec for [base9]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="nonary"} ([b9](#b9){#base9 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base9"}). When we replace the "decimilliday" ([dmd](#dmd){#decimilliday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="decimilliday"}) digit in a [b10](#b10){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base10"} [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} with a [b9](#b9){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base9"} digit, the [b9](#b9){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base9"} digit counts tens of [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"} instead of [dmd](#dmd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="decimilliday"} and the next digit tracks [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"} instead of "centimillidays" ([cmd](#cmd){#centimilliday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="centimillidays"}).
